title: I built a browser strategy game with AI-assisted development. Now I'm wondering how far I can push it.
author: Complete-Moose-4380
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been building a free multiplayer strategy game called [**LinesClash.com**](http://linesclash.com) , using AI coding assistants to help speed up development, testing and iteration.

One of the most interesting parts has been working on the AI opponents.

There are multiple difficulty levels, but Nightmare is where things get interesting. It plays aggressively, punishes mistakes and is genuinely difficult to beat.

The funny part? The opponents don't use LLMs to decide their moves.

I've also added multiplayer, friend challenges and different board sizes.

You can try it here: https://linesclash.com

I'd love some feedback from fellow AI game developers.

Would you introduce LLM-based behaviour into a game like this, or keep the gameplay AI deterministic?

And if you try Nightmare or Experimental, please tell me how it goes 😂

Still learning and improving things every day.
